2607.06214.title: A toy framework for single and multi-agent human-AI curiosity ecosystems
2607.06214.paper_summary: This paper offers a toy framework for considering curiosity as an ecosystem. First, it suggests that a single agent's inquiry policy (how, when, and why an agent asks a question) depends on how the agent values immediate uncertainty reduction, costs, delayed return, and the value of keeping the question open. A key concept in the framework is that the weights on these decision-related terms can change with experience. For example, a period of cheap, quickly answered questions may change the cost of inquiry on a short timescale and change which kinds of questions the agent is drawn to answer over a longer timescale. Second, these ideas are extended to many agents exploring a shared knowledge landscape, and there the framework tracks inquiry volume, topic diversity, frontier-directed inquiry, redundancy, and reusable knowledge. The result is a conceptual toy framework for studying curiosity ecology and for future efforts towards designing multi-agent AI systems for discovery. It serves as a companion piece for a paper currently under review in Trends in Neurosciences.
2607.06214.paper_summary_zh: 這篇論文提供了一個玩具框架，用於將好奇心視為一個生態系統。首先，它建議單一代理的詢問政策（代理如何、何時以及為什麼提出問題）取決於代理對立即不確定性降低、成本、延遲回報以及保持問題開放的價值的評估。該框架中的一個關鍵概念是，這些與決策相關的術語的權重可以隨著經驗而改變。例如，一段時間內便宜且快速回答的問題可能會在短期內改變詢問的成本，並在更長期內改變代理被吸引回答的問題類型。其次，這些想法擴展到多個代理探索共享知識空間，在那裡框架追蹤詢問量、主題多樣性、前沿導向的詢問、冗餘和可重用知識。其結果是一個概念性的玩具框架，用於研究好奇心生態學，以及未來設計多代理AI系統以促進發現的努力。它作為一篇目前正在《神經科學趨勢》期刊審稿中的論文的伴隨作品。
2607.06214.author: Ilya E. Monosov et.al.
